historical_references.context: Kanhaiya is a popular name for Lord Krishna, especially in North India. It is believed that Lord Krishna, being a shepherd, was fond of cows and would often be found playing his flute near the cowsheds. Thus, he is also referred to as Gopala (cowherd) or Govinda (god of cows). The name Kanhaiya is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Kanha' (dark) and 'Iya' (who), translating to 'the dark one'. The name holds a special significance in the Bhakti movement, where devotees often address Lord Krishna as Kanhaiya, and sing his praises through devotional songs, known as bhajans.
